label: a8-01-def-cofinality
tail:
ALLEGATION_VERDICT: REAL_FATAL
ALLEGATION_LOCATION: items/def-cofinality.md lines 10 and 52–54, Regular and singular block
ALLEGATION_ITEM_QUOTE: "**Regular and singular.** An **infinite cardinal**" is immediately followed by "([[def-cardinal]], [[def-aleph-and-beth-hierarchies]]) is".
ALLEGATION_TARGET_QUOTE: items/def-cardinal.md says "Being a cardinal is a property of an ordinal and needs no axiom beyond ZF." items/def-aleph-and-beth-hierarchies.md begins the relevant clause "**Successor and limit cardinals.** An infinite cardinal" and then defines successor and limit cardinals, not infinite cardinal. The uncited items/def-cardinal-arithmetic.md instead begins "**Finite and infinite cardinals.** A cardinal" and explicitly defines when it "is **finite**" and when it is "**infinite**".
ALLEGATION_REASONING: The cited cardinal page defines cardinal but not the finite versus infinite distinction. The cited hierarchy page already assumes the phrase infinite cardinal and defines other notions from it. The exact missing definition is supplied by def-cardinal-arithmetic, which is absent from this item's dependencies and citations. Because infinite cardinal delimits the domain on which regular and singular are being defined, this is a semantically inaccurate citation and a missing direct dependency, not a merely expository gap.

OTHER_FINDINGS: NONE
